title: One key puts the usual transition on the cut at the playhead
goal: In Premiere, Command D puts the default cross dissolve on the cut nearest the playhead, and Final Cut uses Command T. Here a transition needs a click on the cut and a pick from the tiles every time, and Command D deselects. Give the default transition a key, and let a person choose which transition that key uses.
notes: Found by measure-the-video-editor-against-premiere-and-fi (2026-09-24); gap report docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md. Reproduced: command+d on the timeline 'taken by responder chain (Edit > Deselect carries this chord)'. Command T is already taken? Check before picking; the Premiere key is Command D, which collides with Deselect: say in the log which key won and why (Photoshop parity rule: default to Photoshop's for picture keys, Premiere's on the timeline). See also find-out-whether-the-layer-menu-promises-a-dupli (Command D confusion).
acceptance: With the playhead on or near a cut, one key puts the default transition (cross dissolve unless changed) on it, one undo step
The key is printed in the cut's right-click menu and the transition picker
Right-click on a tile in the picker offers Set as Default
A walk cuts a clip, presses the key, and the cut carries a cross dissolve
